core_meaning.meaning_explanation: Ghannam corresponds to the Arabic form غنام (Arabic root غ ن م (gh-n-m); غنّام (Ghannām)). Its core sense is shepherd, keeper of sheep. faq.a: Ghannam is associated with the Arabic form غنام, whose core sense is shepherd, keeper of sheep.

faq.q: What is the origin of Ghannam?
faq.a: Ghannam is associated with Arabic. Ghannam is Arabic غنّام (Ghannām) 'shepherd, keeper of sheep', from غنم (ghanam) 'sheep, livestock'. The source gloss 'traveller, journey' belongs to a different root (س ف ر) and has been replaced.
Yes — the underlying form غنام is Arabic.

faq.q: What does Ghannam mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Ghannam is rendered غنام and carries the sense چرواہا، گلہ بان.

faq.q: What does Ghannam mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Ghannam is rendered غنام and carries the sense چوپان، گله‌بان.
A romanized syllable approximation is ghan-nam. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Ghannam?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Ghannam, ghannam. Script forms are غنام, ग़न्नाम.

faq.q: Is Ghannam a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
